question: Why must a nurse line up the pressure monitor with the phlebostatic axis before reading blood pressure numbers?

options.A: To keep the electronic monitor screen from turning off
options.B: To prevent false high or false low pressure readings
options.C: To make sure the blood sample does not get contaminated
options.D: To stop the arterial line from forming a blood clot

explanation: Leveling the transducer to the right atrium means gravity won't trick your monitor into giving you fake high or low numbers. Accuracy matters!

question: What is a major reason pregnant women might hide their emotional distress from healthcare providers?

options.A: Routine instructions given during antenatal classes
options.B: Complete lack of physical symptoms during gestation
options.C: The absence of hormonal fluctuations in pregnancy
options.D: Fear of being judged and stigmatized as a bad mother

explanation: So true. Stigma makes many mums keep quiet, which is why a warm, non-judgmental nursing approach is so important!

question: What usually happens if a clinic or hospital runs without clear objectives?

options.A: Operational costs drop significantly across all departments.
options.B: Staff morale improves because there is less pressure.
options.C: Patient satisfaction automatically reaches maximum levels.
options.D: Resources are wasted and priorities become unclear.

explanation: Without a clear roadmap, everyone ends up pulling in different directions, leading to wasted time and resources. Clear goals keep the team aligned!

question: Why is activated charcoal often instilled right before the lavage tube is removed?

options.A: To lubricate the tube so it slips out of the throat without friction
options.B: To stimulate normal bowel movements and speed up total digestion
options.C: To neutralize any acidic cleaning fluids remaining in the stomach wall
options.D: To catch and bind any remaining toxin particles left behind in the gut

explanation: Charcoal binds tightly to residual toxins that escaped the physical washing process, preventing them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why are certain medications supplied to the hospital ward in powdered form instead of ready-to-use liquids?

options.A: Powders do not require any mathematical calculations to mix
options.B: Powders have a much longer shelf-life before reconstitution
options.C: Powders can be swallowed directly if the injection fails
options.D: Powders automatically dissolve in normal room air moisture

explanation: Many active drug compounds break down quickly in liquid form. Manufacturers supply them as powders to maintain stability until right before use. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why do nurses use splints and careful positioning for patients with polio?

options.A: To prevent permanent joint contractures and deformities
options.B: To speed up the regeneration of destroyed spinal motor nerves
options.C: To keep the patient completely immobile during ventilation
options.D: To stimulate blood circulation and stop muscle growth

explanation: You got it! When muscles are paralyzed, they pull unevenly. Proper positioning helps keep the joints safe from permanent stiffness.

question: What is the main job of the rugae inside the vaginal canal?

options.A: To constantly secrete lubricating hormones
options.B: To let the vagina stretch wide during childbirth
options.C: To trap bacteria and stop infections
options.D: To produce the monthly period blood

explanation: Well done! Those little folds (rugae) act like an accordion, giving extra tissue so the vagina can safely stretch during delivery.

question: What makes thyroid hormones act a bit differently than other amino acid-derived hormones?

options.A: They are large proteins made of hundreds of linked amino acids
options.B: They only function within the nervous system as fast neurotransmitters
options.C: They cannot travel in the bloodstream without dissolving in red blood cells
options.D: They are fat-soluble and enter cells to bind intracellular receptors

explanation: Even though they start from an amino acid, thyroid hormones behave like fat-loving steroids—they slip right inside the cell to do their work. Tricky, but you'll never forget it now!

question: Why is checking the net fluid balance important after a rectal washout?

options.A: To calculate the exact caloric intake of the patient
options.B: To make sure the patient is not retaining excessive fluid
options.C: To verify the total operating room expenses for the day
options.D: To determine how much medication to give orally

explanation: Comparing how much fluid went in versus how much came out helps you make sure the patient isn't holding onto too much water.

question: A clinic kitchen has a very strict food budget for the month. What is the best way to handle food purchasing?

options.A: Purchase only imported canned goods from abroad
options.B: Buy seasonal local foods that fit the planned menu
options.C: Stop planning meals and buy whatever looks cheapest
options.D: Cut out all protein sources to save money

explanation: Seasonal local foods are usually cheaper, fresher, and align well with planned menus on a tight budget. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h2)

question: A discharged patient calls saying they notice red streaks spreading up their arm from a dog bite. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Apply an ice pack and wait another forty-eight hours
options.B: Stop taking the antibiotics because the red streaks are normal
options.C: Wash the arm with scented soap and increase fluid intake
options.D: Return to the emergency department immediately for evaluation

explanation: Spreading red streaks suggest a fast-moving infection like lymphangitis. This requires prompt medical re-evaluation right away!

question: Why is teaching the patient properly before a barium enema so important?

options.A: It means they won't need any physical check in the radiology room
options.B: It stops all belly discomfort during the test
options.C: It ensures they clean their colon properly so leftover stool doesn't ruin the X-ray
options.D: It completely cures their bowel disease before the test starts

explanation: If stool is left in the colon, it can look just like a tumor on the X-ray. Good prep prevents wrong results!

question: A patient starts a new antidepressant and soon reports she cannot achieve orgasm, even though she still has normal desire. Which category fits this best?

options.A: Substance/Medication-Induced Sexual Dysfunction
options.B: Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder
options.C: Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder
options.D: Primary lifelong orgasmic dysfunction

explanation: Well done! Because the symptom popped up right after starting a specific medication, we link it directly to that substance.

question: Why is a high D-dimer blood result worrying in a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: It shows that the kidneys are failing to filter waste
options.B: It suggests an increased risk for abnormal blood clot formation
options.C: It proves the patient has a severe bacterial lung infection
options.D: It indicates permanent damage to the heart muscle valves

explanation: Well done! D-dimer is a protein left behind when clots break down. High levels mean the body is forming clots somewhere it shouldn't.

question: When is the best time for a nurse to screen a patient for gender-based violence?

options.A: Only after the patient asks for police assistance
options.B: Exclusively during annual national health campaigns
options.C: Privately and routinely during clinical assessments
options.D: Loudly in a crowded waiting room for everyone to hear

explanation: Brilliant! Screening must always happen in a private, confidential space so the patient feels safe enough to open up to you.

question: A patient with cardiogenic shock and fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema) is admitted. Why should you avoid giving large, fast IV fluid boluses?

options.A: It triggers an immediate allergic reaction in cardiac tissue
options.B: It will immediately cause severe peripheral vasoconstriction
options.C: It can worsen heart failure and increase fluid buildup in the lungs
options.D: It interferes with the accurate reading of arterial blood gases

explanation: In cardiogenic shock, the heart pump itself is failing. Pouring more fluids into a tired heart is like trying to pump water through a jammed engine—it just backs up into the lungs!

question: Why do nurses calculate a patient's BMI?

options.A: To quickly screen for weight categories and health risks
options.B: To diagnose heart and metabolic diseases directly
options.C: To calculate exact daily food calories
options.D: To measure exact body fat percentage in muscles

explanation: BMI is a quick screening tool to help you spot weight categories that could lead to health issues. You're doing great!

question: When does the debriefing session take place in the simulation learning cycle?

options.A: Before the students even read their patient charts
options.B: Immediately after the simulation scenario finishes
options.C: Only when a student fails a practical examination
options.D: Several weeks after the clinical rotation is finished

explanation: Debriefing happens right after the scenario while the events and emotions are still fresh in the students' minds. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal emotional challenge many women face during pregnancy?

options.A: Mood swings driven by profound hormonal shifts
options.B: Heightened anxiety about the upcoming labor process
options.C: Stress regarding financial changes and parenting duties
options.D: Complete emotional numbness and lack of heartbeat awareness

explanation: Well spotted! Mood swings, stress, and anxiety are totally normal with pregnancy hormones, but complete emotional numbness is not a typical response.

question: Which strategy best combines behaviorist and constructivist approaches in nursing school?

options.A: Focusing solely on the emotional well-being of students during exam weeks
options.B: Relying exclusively on silent reading assignments and standardized multiple-choice quizzes
options.C: Using skills checklists for procedural accuracy alongside simulation scenarios for clinical reasoning
options.D: Allowing students to do whatever clinical tasks they prefer without any supervision

explanation: Checklists help nail down precise steps (behaviorism), while simulation scenarios let you problem-solve and build deep understanding (constructivism). Perfect combo!

question: What is one of the most serious risks when an older adult suffers a fall?

options.A: Severe injury and potential loss of independence
options.B: Permanent immunity from future joint pain
options.C: Immediate improvement in their overall balance
options.D: An automatic increase in their muscle strength

explanation: Falls can lead to broken bones and a lasting fear of falling again, which often strips away an older adult's ability to care for themselves.

question: Why are Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) most effective when used while sleeping?

options.A: Anopheles mosquitoes bite mostly at night when people are asleep
options.B: It prevents mosquitoes from laying eggs inside household water pots
options.C: The chemical on the net repels daytime flies and cockroaches
options.D: It completely stops the flow of humid air into the bedroom

explanation: You got it! Since malaria mosquitoes love to hunt during the night, sleeping under a treated net hits them right when they are most active.

question: At what point in the patient's hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?

options.A: Two hours before leaving
options.B: After arriving back home
options.C: During the final doctor's round
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Discharge planning starts early so the care team has enough time to arrange equipment, home support, and education before the patient leaves. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: Who is widely recognized as America's first trained psychiatric nurse?

options.A: Linda Richards
options.B: Mary Seacole
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Clara Barton

explanation: Linda Richards paved the way! She pushed hard for specialized training so nurses could better care for patients with mental health needs.

question: What happens when a hospital fails to accurately calculate the cost of its nursing services?

options.A: Patients receive too many medications
options.B: It struggles to set fair prices and manage budgets
options.C: Doctors refuse to admit new patients
options.D: The hospital building loses structural value

explanation: If you don't know what your services actually cost, it's impossible to set fair prices or keep the hospital financially healthy.

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in your nervous system?

options.A: To send final motor commands to skeletal muscles
options.B: To produce hormones that regulate body temperature
options.C: To monitor changes inside and outside the body
options.D: To integrate information inside the spinal cord

explanation: You've got this! Sensory receptors are like your body's watchmen—they catch what's happening around and inside you and report it back to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h1)

question: Which clotting protein increases a lot during pregnancy to prepare for childbirth?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Bilirubin
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Fibrinogen

explanation: Fibrinogen is a key player in blood clotting. It rises nicely during pregnancy to protect the mother from heavy bleeding during delivery.

question: Why should a nurse apply pressure to an IV site immediately after withdrawing the catheter?

options.A: To ensure the plastic catheter tip remains intact inside the arm.
options.B: To push any remaining trapped air bubbles back up into the vein.
options.C: To stimulate rapid skin healing and eliminate scarring completely.
options.D: To stop bleeding and prevent hematoma formation at the site.

explanation: Applying direct pressure helps seal the puncture wound in the blood vessel wall, stopping external bleeding and preventing internal bruising. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h8)

question: On a histogram, what does the vertical axis (Y-axis) usually stand for?

options.A: The individual patient identification numbers
options.B: The specific names of nursing units
options.C: The frequency or count of observations
options.D: The calendar dates of data collection

explanation: Think of the Y-axis as the counter: it tells you how many times a certain value or range popped up.

question: What is evaluated during a functional assessment prior to admission?

options.A: Financial credit history
options.B: Workplace performance record
options.C: Previous travel experiences
options.D: Activities of daily living

explanation: A functional assessment looks closely at how well a potential resident can manage basic daily self-care tasks like bathing and dressing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team (doctors, nurses, physiotherapists) so important for patients with advanced disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Physicians are not permitted to manage neurological disorders alone
options.B: The disease affects many different physical, cognitive, and emotional functions
options.C: It eliminates the need for any ongoing medical drug therapy
options.D: Patients require daily surgical procedures to replace damaged nerves

explanation: Because MS touches movement, speech, mood, and daily living, it takes a whole team of specialists working together to give the patient the best quality of life.

question: Why do regular smokers need to smoke more over time to feel the same buzz?

options.A: Their lungs have expanded and require more volume
options.B: Their social circles encourage heavier smoking habits
options.C: Their brains have developed tolerance to the chemical
options.D: The tobacco companies put weaker ingredients in newer packs

explanation: Tolerance happens when the brain gets so used to nicotine that it needs higher amounts to feel that same initial effect. Great job thinking this through!

question: A patient from a Nigerian riverine community has a bloody cough after eating local crabs. Which cooking method failed to protect them?

options.A: Steaming the crab over an open flame until fully done
options.B: Boiling the whole crab for thirty minutes
options.C: Marinating the crab meat in local lime juice
options.D: Frying the crustacean in hot palm oil until crisp

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Acidic marinades like lime juice add great flavor, but they do not reliably kill tough parasite cysts. Only thorough heat can do that!

question: What is the main goal of studying 'human factors' in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of night shifts a nurse can work
options.B: Punishing nurses who make mistakes during medication rounds
options.C: Reducing the salary costs of hospital administrative staff
options.D: Matching clinical work systems to human strengths and limits

explanation: You've got this! Human factors simply looks at how we interact with our workplace so we can design safer, easier systems—instead of just blaming people when things go wrong.

question: Why is a hormone profile including FSH, LH, and testosterone ordered during a male infertility workup?

options.A: To measure the exact temperature inside the scrotal sac
options.B: To check if pre-testicular endocrine imbalances are causing poor sperm production
options.C: To screen the patient for genetic chromosomal translocations
options.D: To confirm the presence of a physical blockage inside the vas deferens

explanation: Hormone blood tests show whether the brain and endocrine system are properly signaling the testicles to make sperm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: Which of these is a clear example of an unsafe injection habit?

options.A: Using a contaminated needle to enter a single-dose medication vial
options.B: Using a fresh, sterile needle and syringe for every single patient
options.C: Dropping a used syringe straight into a safety box
options.D: Cleaning the skin with an alcohol swab before the poke

explanation: Never use a needle that has touched a surface or a patient to draw more medicine. It contaminates the whole vial and puts the next person in danger.

question: Which sleep disorder involves the upper airway repeatedly collapsing while a person sleeps?

options.A: Primary insomnia
options.B: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.C: Restless legs syndrome
options.D: Narcolepsy

explanation: In obstructive sleep apnea, throat muscles relax too much during sleep and temporarily block airflow, causing the person to briefly wake up to breathe.

question: What is venepuncture primarily used for in clinical practice?

options.A: Withdrawing blood for diagnostic testing
options.B: Checking lung function capacity
options.C: Assessing electrical heart activity
options.D: Measuring deep body temperature

explanation: Venepuncture involves piercing a vein to collect blood samples needed for various laboratory investigations. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient on a ventilator has low oxygen and is straining their neck muscles just to breathe. What's the best nursing diagnosis here?

options.A: Impaired Social Interaction
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Constipation
options.D: Ineffective Breathing Pattern

explanation: Spot on! When you see a patient working way too hard with their accessory muscles and struggling for oxygen, their breathing pattern is definitely ineffective and needs your help.

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask patients about herbal supplements during a medication history?

options.A: Herbal remedies cannot cause any harm or adverse reactions.
options.B: Supplements are strictly regulated by the government for safety.
options.C: Herbal products and supplements can also trigger idiosyncratic reactions.
options.D: Patients only take herbal supplements when prescription drugs fail.

explanation: Never underestimate herbs! Traditional supplements contain active chemicals just like prescription drugs, meaning they can cause unexpected reactions too.

question: Which inner ear structure detects when you spin or turn your head?

options.A: Cochlea
options.B: Semicircular canals
options.C: Eustachian tube
options.D: Tympanic membrane

explanation: You've got this! The three semicircular canals sit at different angles to catch motion whenever you turn your head in any direction.

question: Where inside a liver cell do you mostly find the famous Cytochrome P450 enzymes?

options.A: Nucleus of red blood cells
options.B: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum of liver cells
options.C: Cell membrane of skeletal muscle tissue
options.D: Mitochondria of the brain

explanation: These hardworking CYP450 enzymes hang out densely packed in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum of liver cells (hepatocytes). They do the heavy lifting of drug breakdown!

question: Which health worker is primarily responsible for managing complex surgical deliveries in the team?

options.A: Obstetrician/Gynecologist
options.B: Pharmacy technician
options.C: Midwife
options.D: Community Health Extension Worker

explanation: An obstetrician is a physician specialist trained to handle complex surgical interventions like cesarean sections. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why is a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment broader than a standard physical examination?

options.A: It is only performed by hospital administrators to calculate medical bills
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory investigations and blood tests entirely
options.C: It focuses exclusively on surgical interventions for severe joint injuries
options.D: It evaluates social, psychological, and functional factors alongside physical health

explanation: Older adults have interconnected health and social needs, so a CGA looks at the whole person and their environment, not just their disease. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h4)

question: During a health emergency, how do health ministries use surveillance data?

options.A: To allocate scarce medical resources where they are needed most
options.B: To select which nursing students receive scholarships
options.C: To decide which private hospitals should be closed permanently
options.D: To determine salary increases for hospital administrators

explanation: Good data shows us exactly where an outbreak is hitting hardest. That way, we can rush medications, supplies, and staff right where they'll save the most lives.

question: Why do community health nurses love using the Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) tape in the field?

options.A: It is quick, easy to use, and does not require complex scales
options.B: It is the only tool that can accurately measure linear height in toddlers
options.C: It gives an exact measurement of the child's total body fat percentage
options.D: It replaces the need to check for clinical signs of vitamin deficiency

explanation: Exactly! MUAC is portable, fast, and practical when you are out in community outreaches screening lots of children quickly.

question: Why is self-medication so common across Nigeria?

options.A: Standard hospitals rarely stock basic pain relief tablets
options.B: People prefer reading package leaflets over talking to doctors
options.C: Hospital queues, costs, and easy access to open-air drug markets drive the practice
options.D: The government mandates that every citizen treat themselves first

explanation: You got it! Long wait times at clinics and financial constraints often push people to easily accessible informal drug vendors instead.

question: What is the core philosophy of family-centered care in pediatrics?

options.A: Viewing the family as an essential partner in the child's healthcare
options.B: Focusing exclusively on hospital-based procedures
options.C: Excluding family members from daily medical decisions
options.D: Treating the child without input from the parents

explanation: Family-centered care builds on the strengths of families and honors their central role in the child's life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended home care practice for managing a mild fever?

options.A: Giving prescribed doses of antipyretic medication safely
options.B: Monitoring the patient for unusual symptoms or confusion
options.C: Dressing the patient in heavy, thick blankets to trap body heat
options.D: Encouraging frequent oral intake of fluids and water

explanation: Trapping body heat with heavy blankets prevents natural cooling and can cause the temperature to rise even higher. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the usual maximum flow rate recommended for a standard nasal cannula?

options.A: 2 Liters per minute
options.B: 12 Liters per minute
options.C: 20 Liters per minute
options.D: 6 Liters per minute

explanation: We usually stick to 1 to 6 Liters per minute for standard cannulas. Going higher mostly just dries out the nose without giving extra benefits.

question: What is the primary goal of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To give the doctor time to finish other ward rounds
options.B: To test the patient's memory and cognitive function
options.C: To reduce anxiety and help them adjust to the new environment
options.D: To ensure the patient fills out their discharge papers early

explanation: A good orientation helps a frightened or stressed patient feel secure by showing them how things work around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is a huge advantage of molecular tests over traditional lab cultures?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need to collect any patient specimen
options.B: They allow the nurse to administer antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.C: They can identify germs much faster without waiting days for colonies to grow
options.D: They are always much cheaper than any other laboratory test

explanation: Great job! Molecular tests look straight at the DNA, saving us from waiting days for bacteria to grow in a dish.

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs
options.B: Engage the men in respectful dialogue, emphasizing child spacing, maternal health, and family financial stability
options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being.

question: Why do heart conditions often lead to dangerous electrical rhythm problems?

options.A: The brain sends extra electricity to the chest on purpose
options.B: Heart valves open and close too softly
options.C: Red blood cells carry too much oxygen to the nodes
options.D: Damaged or scarred heart muscle messes up normal electrical pathways

explanation: Electricity needs a smooth road to travel. When scar tissue or lack of oxygen damages the heart muscle, the electrical signals get blocked or go haywire, causing erratic heartbeats.

question: In nursing, what do we actually mean when we say a patient or student has 'learned' something?

options.A: A permanent change in behavior resulting from experience
options.B: Reading hospital policy manuals before starting a shift
options.C: Memorizing medical terminology for board examinations
options.D: Listening passively to a doctor during ward rounds

explanation: Learning isn't just cramming for a test—it's when new knowledge or practice genuinely sticks and changes how you do things!

question: Which of these is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated hyperemesis?

options.A: Intestinal growth restriction
options.B: Low birth weight
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Preterm birth

explanation: Heart defects happen during early structural development, whereas hyperemesis baby issues are usually about poor nutrition and low birth weight. You're mastering neonatal risks!

question: What is the main purpose of gentle stretching exercises in degenerative disorders?

options.A: To cure underlying nerve damage
options.B: To increase overall bone length
options.C: To reverse muscle wasting completely
options.D: To prevent painful joint contractures

explanation: Gentle stretching keeps joints flexible and helps stop the painful tightening of muscles and tendons known as contractures. You are mastering this!

question: When would a nurse researcher build a conceptual framework instead of using a single theoretical framework?

options.A: When combining ideas from multiple sources to fit a unique study
options.B: When the researcher wants to avoid reading published literature
options.C: When the study has no human participants involved
options.D: When the hospital administration bans the use of theories

explanation: Sometimes one theory isn't enough! When your study has a unique mix of ideas, you blend them together into your own custom conceptual framework.

question: What is the best nursing action when taking care of a patient with a bleeding disorder?

options.A: Checking core body temperature using a rectal thermometer
options.B: Applying direct pressure to venipuncture sites for an extended time
options.C: Administering all routine medications via intramuscular injection
options.D: Encouraging participation in high-contact competitive sports

explanation: Giving a little extra pressure after drawing blood or giving an injection gives that soft platelet plug enough time to form and prevents nasty bruises (hematomas)!

question: How would you score a patient who speaks in full sentences, but insists they are in a different city and year?

options.A: Incomprehensible sounds
options.B: Confused conversation
options.C: Inappropriate words
options.D: Oriented and alert

explanation: Even though they are talking in sentences, getting the place and time wrong means they are confused. They get a verbal score of 4 for confused conversation.

question: A mother in labor suddenly starts having severe seizures from pre-eclampsia at a rural clinic. Which emergency drug should you give?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Routine prenatal vitamins
options.C: Injectable iron sucrose
options.D: Normal saline tablets

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the gold-standard emergency medication for stopping and preventing dangerous eclamptic seizures.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse within the multidisciplinary palliative care team?

options.A: Making all final medical diagnoses and prescribing drugs alone
options.B: Replacing the family members during visiting hours
options.C: Acting as a central hub of communication and coordinating care
options.D: Handling the financial billing and insurance claims for the hospital

explanation: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside, making them uniquely positioned to coordinate input from all team members. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h8)

question: Where do school health programs mainly take place?

options.A: Local community primary health centers
options.B: Educational institutions and classrooms
options.C: State-managed regional hospitals
options.D: Private pediatric specialty clinics

explanation: You got it! School health programs focus on schools because that's where children spend most of their day learning and growing.

question: Why do lab scientists often prefer molecular genetic tests over traditional culture methods for tricky microbes?

options.A: Genetic tests are always performed at the patient bedside by nurses
options.B: Molecular methods eliminate the need for any laboratory safety equipment
options.C: Culture methods cannot tell the difference between bacteria and viruses
options.D: Molecular methods identify organisms directly from genetic material without slow culture growth

explanation: Growing germs in a culture dish can take agonizingly days or weeks. Molecular tests find the DNA directly, giving quick answers when patients need care fast!

question: How does community MHPSS nursing differ from traditional hospital-based psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It forbids the nurse from ever talking to the patient's family members
options.B: It replaces the need for medical doctors in emergency situations
options.C: It extends beyond hospital walls to train primary workers and promote mental health
options.D: It focuses solely on locking ward doors and managing physical restraints

explanation: Community nursing means stepping out of the ward! You get to educate, mentor local health workers, and promote wellness right where people live.

question: How should a nurse manager respond to an employee who engages in at-risk behavior, such as taking a minor shortcut because of heavy workload?

options.A: Ignore the action completely as long as no one died.
options.B: Fire the nurse instantly without a hearing.
options.C: Report the nurse to the police for criminal charges.
options.D: Coach the nurse and evaluate the underlying system pressure.

explanation: At-risk behavior involves choices where risk is misunderstood or normalized, so it requires coaching and workflow evaluation rather than harsh punishment. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the medical term for seeing double, which happens when the nerves controlling eye movement are messed up?

options.A: Mydriasis
options.B: Ptosis
options.C: Diplopia
options.D: Strabismus

explanation: Diplopia is just the clinical word for double vision. It occurs when the tiny muscles around the eyes aren't working together smoothly.

question: What factor can significantly alter a child's vital sign readings during a home assessment?

options.A: The time of the family meal
options.B: The brand of soap used at home
options.C: Crying or anxiety
options.D: The color of the bedroom wall

explanation: Correct! Fear, anxiety, or crying can cause a child's heart rate and breathing to jump up temporarily. Always keep that in mind during assessments! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h3)

question: How can rural communities creatively solve the problem of getting sick patients to a clinic?

options.A: Organizing local emergency transport systems like tricycles
options.B: Waiting for ambulances to be stationed in every street
options.C: Demanding that the government buy cars for every family
options.D: Building major federal highways to connect every village

explanation: Spot on! Communities often band together to arrange local transport like branded tricycles or bikes to bridge the gap during emergencies.

question: What actually happens during a heart attack (myocardial infarction)?

question: A mother exclusively breastfeeding her four-month-old baby notices her monthly period just returned. What should you advise her about LAM?

question: What is the best way for a nurse administrator to handle a valid complaint about poor hospital services?

question: Which measurements do nurses routinely track to monitor a patient's progress on a low-calorie diet?

question: Why is brainstem damage usually more life-threatening than an injury to the cerebral cortex?

question: What is a common health vulnerability frequently faced by single-parent households?

question: Why is a pregnancy test almost always ordered when a patient arrives with lower belly pain and suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To confirm that the patient is currently using hormonal contraceptives
options.B: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy, which can present with similar pain
options.C: To measure baseline kidney function before starting antibiotic therapy
options.D: To check if high hormone levels caused the bacterial overgrowth

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy is a medical emergency that can mimic pelvic infection pain, so nurses always check this first to keep the patient safe.

question: Which test is commonly used to screen for too much adrenaline breakdown in a suspected pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Morning serum cortisol levels
options.B: Serum fasting blood glucose
options.C: 24-hour urinary metanephrines
options.D: Serum electrolyte panel

explanation: Collecting urine over 24 hours lets us measure metanephrines, which are the leftover waste products of extra adrenaline and noradrenaline over a full day.

question: Which serious lung condition is a major emergency for a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Acute chest syndrome
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Acute chest syndrome involves lung infection and tissue damage, bringing chest pain and fever that needs fast medical care.

question: Why do nursing students still need to learn traditional medication abbreviations?

options.A: Older paper charts and verbal orders still use them
options.B: Hospitals legally require staff to write in Latin shorthand
options.C: Computers cannot process plain English medication names
options.D: Using abbreviations prevents all forms of medical errors

explanation: Spot on! Even though things are modernizing, you'll still see these shorthand terms on older paper notes and hear experienced clinicians use them on the ward.

question: What is a major public health challenge linked to teenage pregnancies?

options.A: Immediate onset of chronic hypertension
options.B: Permanent cessation of natural bone growth
options.C: Decreased overall societal life expectancy
options.D: Increased maternal morbidity and mortality

explanation: Complications from early childbirth and unsafe procedures are major reasons young mothers face serious health risks. You've got this!

question: How do community support groups help individuals living with diabetes?

options.A: By supplying free prescription medications to every attendee
options.B: By reducing isolation and sharing practical coping strategies
options.C: By diagnosing new medical complications before doctors do
options.D: By replacing professional nursing care with traditional remedies

explanation: Support groups offer emotional encouragement and practical advice from peers who truly understand the daily realities of living with a chronic illness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)

question: Why do nurses give routine immunizations to patients?

options.A: To stimulate adaptive immunity and build long-term memory cells
options.B: To instantly kill any bacteria currently residing in the bloodstream
options.C: To trigger an immediate innate response via localized vasodilation
options.D: To replace missing white blood cells in immunosuppressed clients

explanation: You're doing great! Vaccines give a safe preview of a germ so your adaptive system can build memory cells for future protection.

question: Why is establishing cause and effect difficult in cross-sectional studies?

options.A: Statistical software cannot process percentages
options.B: Researchers always interview too few patients
options.C: Exposure and outcome are measured at the same time
options.D: Participants never answer questionnaires honestly

explanation: Since you check both the risk factor and the health issue at the exact same moment, it's tough to know which one happened first.

question: Which metabolic pathway breaks down large molecules and releases energy?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Anabolism
options.C: Osmosis
options.D: Catabolism

explanation: Remember: Catabolism cuts things down! It tears complex molecules into simpler pieces, releasing energy for your body to use. Easy peasy!

question: Proteus mirabilis is a type of bacteria strongly linked with which urinary problem?

options.A: Severe hypertension
options.B: Glomerular destruction
options.C: Kidney stone formation
options.D: Prostatic hypertrophy

explanation: Proteus produces a special enzyme that changes urine chemistry, making it easier for painful kidney stones (struvite stones) to form. Good to know in clinical practice!

question: A patient with severe arthritis in one knee gets a direct steroid injection into the joint. What is the main benefit?

options.A: It lets the drug bypass the liver to enter the brain instantly.
options.B: It gives high drug concentration at the problem site while sparing the rest of the body.
options.C: It completely cures the underlying autoimmune disease.
options.D: It guarantees no side effects like high blood pressure.

explanation: Correct! Giving the injection right into the knee treats the local pain while keeping whole-body side effects as low as possible.

question: What is one of the biggest challenges children with special needs often face in our communities?

options.A: Higher risk of social isolation and stigma
options.B: Automatic placement in boarding schools
options.C: Immediate independence in all life activities
options.D: Guaranteed immunity from childhood infections

explanation: Societal misunderstandings can unfortunately cause children with special needs to face isolation and stigma. As nurses, our warmth and acceptance help break down these barriers!

question: What does a null hypothesis usually claim?

options.A: There is no real difference or effect between the groups.
options.B: All patients in the sample will experience full recovery.
options.C: The new nursing intervention is better than the old one.
options.D: The study sample was too small to draw any conclusions.

explanation: You got it! The null hypothesis is like saying 'nothing special is happening here; any difference is just by chance.' It's the starting point for testing!

question: What is the main root cause behind gender-based violence?

options.A: Genetics and hereditary health disorders
options.B: Temporary financial stress in families
options.C: Lack of formal education in victims
options.D: Unequal power dynamics between genders

explanation: Spot on! Gender-based violence usually stems from imbalances of power between men and women in society, rather than just money troubles or genetics.

question: Which laboratory blood test is considered the most reliable routine marker for estimating the Glomerular Filtration Rate?

options.A: Serum creatinine
options.B: Total serum protein
options.C: Serum potassium
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: Creatinine levels rise when kidney filtration slows down, making it the standard lab marker for evaluating renal function. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h7)

question: How do standard expectorants typically trigger increased fluid secretion in the lungs?

options.A: By stopping the production of white blood cells in the chest
options.B: By mildly irritating the gastric mucosa to trigger reflex pathways
options.C: By directly binding to receptors on the surface of lung alveoli
options.D: By freezing the mucus so it cracks and breaks apart easily

explanation: It's a clever body trick! Traditional expectorants cause a tiny bit of irritation in the stomach, which sends a reflex signal to the respiratory glands to release more watery fluid.

question: In public health and community nursing, what age range defines the "girl child"?

options.A: From puberty to twenty-one years
options.B: From birth to twelve years
options.C: From infancy to five years
options.D: From birth to eighteen years

explanation: You'll often hear this in community postings! The girl child covers females from the day they are born until they turn 18, right before legal adulthood. You've got this!

question: Why do veteran staff members often resist changes to workplace culture?

options.A: A strong desire to take on extra administrative responsibilities
options.B: An eagerness to learn brand new hospital software programs
options.C: Excessive financial compensation for participating in committees
options.D: Fear of the unknown and attachment to established habits

explanation: You're right! People naturally feel uneasy about change when they are comfortable with familiar routines and unsure how new rules will impact them.

question: What do we call a person who carries a disease-causing germ without showing any signs of illness?

options.A: A host
options.B: A vector
options.C: A fomite
options.D: A carrier

explanation: Carriers look and feel healthy, making them dangerous because they can spread infections without anyone realizing it. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h2)

question: How is 'prevalence' different from 'incidence'?

options.A: Prevalence only counts patients who are currently hospitalized
options.B: Prevalence includes all existing cases, both old and new
options.C: Prevalence is only used for vaccine trial evaluations
options.D: Prevalence measures how fast a disease spreads in a week

explanation: While incidence is just the *new* cases, prevalence is the grand total of everyone currently living with the condition (old and new together). Easy peasy!

question: Why is finding the root cause so important before choosing a health intervention?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by the federal ministry of health
options.B: It stops community members from asking too many questions
options.C: It ensures you treat the real source of the issue rather than just the symptoms
options.D: It guarantees that funding will double for the project

explanation: Brilliant! Finding the root cause stops us from wasting energy on surface fixes while the real problem keeps hurting the community. Smart nursing thinking!

question: Which community action has the best long-term impact on controlling contact infections?

options.A: Promoting personal hygiene and discouraging the sharing of towels and clothing
options.B: Providing free multivitamins to every household once a year
options.C: Sprinkling strong chemical insecticides on all open community grounds
options.D: Isolating all infected community members in distant rural camps

explanation: Education is key! Teaching communities good hygiene habits stops outbreaks right at the roots so they don't keep coming back.

question: What is a major challenge to good communication in busy Nigerian clinics?

options.A: The complete absence of cultural traditions
options.B: An oversupply of advanced diagnostic equipment
options.C: Heavy patient loads and understaffed facilities
options.D: Mandatory communication training for all staff

explanation: True! When clinics are overcrowded and nurses are rushed, it becomes so easy to slip into commanding or hurried communication.

question: What is the main purpose of adding a small 'sustainability mark-up' to DRF drugs?

options.A: To pay the personal salaries of the hospital medical director
options.B: To protect the fund against inflation, wastage, and future stock depletion
options.C: To generate heavy profits for private investors
options.D: To punish patients who do not pay their hospital bills on time

explanation: The sustainability margin acts as a safety cushion against rising market prices and expired items so the fund doesn't shrink.

question: How does actively absorbing sodium from the gut affect fluid movement?

options.A: It destroys water molecules to prevent severe dehydration
options.B: It draws water out of the lumen and into the mucosal cells
options.C: It repels water molecules and forces them into the stool
options.D: It keeps water trapped inside the lumen until digestion finishes

explanation: Exactly! Pumping sodium out of the gut space creates an osmotic pull that drags water right along with it into the body tissues.

question: As a nurse, why should you avoid telling a panicked patient that 'everything will be fine'?

options.A: It violates standard hospital communication policy
options.B: It offers false reassurance that cannot be guaranteed
options.C: It forces the patient to become overly talkative
options.D: It increases the patient's heart rate immediately

explanation: Well done! Since we can't predict the future, promising that 'everything will be fine' can break trust if things take a turn. Honest, gentle grounding is always safer.

question: A child with cerebral palsy presents with very stiff muscles and hyperactive reflexes. Which type of cerebral palsy is this child most likely experiencing?

options.A: Ataxic
options.B: Dyskinetic
options.C: Flaccid
options.D: Spastic

explanation: Spastic cerebral palsy is marked by increased muscle tone and exaggerated reflexes because of injury to the motor cortex or pyramidal tracts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h3)

question: What does a dermatome represent in physical assessment?

options.A: A reflex arc located in the lower spine
options.B: The protective covering around the spinal cord
options.C: An area of skin supplied by a single spinal nerve
options.D: A group of muscles controlled by one motor nerve

explanation: A dermatome is a skin segment that receives its sensory innervation from one specific spinal nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h8)

question: A nurse needs to inform the shift team about a new hospital policy change. What is the best way to use group communication for this?

options.A: Send a secure group message or email to all staff members on the ward
options.B: Write the policy on a random patient whiteboard in the main hallway
options.C: Share the details on a personal social media account without privacy filters
options.D: Call every single staff member individually during their busy morning rounds

explanation: Group messaging allows charge nurses to efficiently broadcast general updates and policy changes to an entire team at once. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do we need teamwork across different professions (like nurses, fire service, and police) during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: Different agencies bring specialized skills that must be synchronized to save lives.
options.B: It ensures that nurses never have to make independent clinical decisions.
options.C: Paramedics and firefighters do not work well unless supervised by nurses.
options.D: Hospital administrators are the only ones qualified to handle patient triage.

explanation: Exactly right! No single profession has all the answers, so police, fire, and medical teams must join forces as one unit.

question: What is a key focus when nursing an expectant mother who has chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Administering prophylactic dialysis starting in the first trimester
options.B: Strict blood pressure monitoring and medication adherence support
options.C: Restricting fluid intake entirely to prevent maternal edema
options.D: Encouraging a high-protein diet to replace lost urinary nutrients

explanation: Keeping blood pressure in check takes the pressure off the kidneys and keeps the placenta happy and well-supplied with blood.

question: How do modern nutritional guidelines differ from the ones created in the early 20th century?

options.A: They now focus on preventing chronic diseases in addition to stopping deficiencies
options.B: They have completely removed any guidelines regarding vitamins and minerals
options.C: They only focus on calculating the exact amount of daily calories needed
options.D: They are designed exclusively for treating severe hospital patients

explanation: You got it! While older guidelines just wanted to stop diseases like rickets, today we also look at long-term wellness, like preventing heart disease and obesity.

question: What is '360-degree feedback' in a nursing performance review?

options.A: Asking the head of nursing to observe a nurse from all angles
options.B: Rotating a nurse through every department in the hospital for a day
options.C: Gathering performance input from peers, patients, and other team members
options.D: Measuring how many degrees a nurse can bend during physical therapy

explanation: Think of it as getting the full picture! Instead of just your boss judging you, feedback comes from colleagues, patients, and doctors who work closely with you.

question: A client in a Nigerian teaching hospital demands to see their medical case notes after a surgery. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Facilitate access to the medical records following the hospital's proper administrative process
options.B: Refuse firmly because hospital files belong exclusively to the doctors and nurses
options.C: Burn the records immediately to protect the privacy of the surgical team
options.D: Tell the client that reading medical notes is illegal for ordinary citizens

explanation: Clients have the legal right to view their own medical records through the established institutional procedures. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: What is a very common side effect of post-surgical pain medications that ruins a patient's appetite?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Rapid hair growth
options.C: Increased muscle mass
options.D: Constipation

explanation: Right! Pain medicines like opioids slow down the bowels, causing stubborn constipation that kills appetite and brings on nausea.

question: What is the normal pH range of the skin's protective acid mantle?
explanation: Well done! A slightly acidic pH between 4.5 and 5.5 makes it hard for harmful bacteria and fungi to grow on us. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h3)

question: Before puberty starts, what does the central nervous system usually do regarding reproductive hormones?

options.A: It produces excess adult levels
options.B: It completely shuts down the pituitary
options.C: It suppresses hormone release
options.D: It secretes erratic daily spikes

explanation: You got it! Throughout childhood, the brain actively keeps reproductive hormone levels low and quiet until the body is mature enough for puberty.

question: Which hormone directly builds up and thickens the uterine lining during the first half of the cycle?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Think of estrogen as the builder hormone! Produced by the growing follicles, it helps rebuild and thicken the endometrium after a period ends.

question: Why do standard precautions apply to every single patient in the ward, even those not diagnosed with an infection?

options.A: Patients get offended if healthcare workers wear gloves only for some beds
options.B: Some patients may carry infections without showing any symptoms yet
options.C: Hospital management requires it only for statistical record keeping
options.D: It is too difficult for nurses to remember different rules for different people

explanation: Standard precautions assume any body fluid can carry pathogens because asymptomatic carriers can transmit infections unknowingly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: What does the frequency column in a distribution table tell a researcher?

options.A: The total number of missing patient files
options.B: The mathematical average of the dataset
options.C: How many times a specific value occurs
options.D: The exact date the data was collected

explanation: Frequency simply counts the number of times a particular score, category, or observation appears in the dataset. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h4)

question: A young female patient is treated for chlamydia. What crucial step must you take as a nurse to prevent the infection from coming back?

options.A: Advise her to avoid all physical exercise for six months
options.B: Schedule immediate surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.C: Ensure her sexual partners are also evaluated and treated
options.D: Prescribe long-term daily hormonal contraceptive pills

explanation: You nailed it! Treating partners stops the back-and-forth spread of infection and keeps your patient safe from repeated pelvic inflammation. Great clinical thinking!

question: Why is recording baseline vital signs and functional ability on the initial assessment sheet important?

options.A: It proves to the family that the nurse arrived on time
options.B: It provides a starting point to measure future clinical progress or decline
options.C: It allows the nurse to discharge the client immediately on day one
options.D: It satisfies administrative paperwork without affecting daily nursing care

explanation: Baseline data gives the nurse a clear point of comparison to see if treatments are working or if the client's health is worsening. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is a low-sodium diet commonly prescribed for a patient with heart failure?

options.A: To increase the speed at which food digests in the gut.
options.B: To reduce fluid retention and ease the workload on the heart.
options.C: To help the kidneys produce more red blood cells.
options.D: To prevent the patient from developing an upset stomach.

explanation: Sodium causes the body to hold onto water; restricting it prevents fluid buildup, which lowers the strain on a weakened heart. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h7)

question: What is the main reason for doing regular physical stock counts in a pharmacy?

options.A: To compare actual pills on the shelf with recorded ledger numbers
options.B: To calculate the annual bonus for the hospital accountant
options.C: To make the pharmacy staff work longer hours on the weekend
options.D: To dispose of all medications that have been on the shelf for one week

explanation: Counting actual stock helps catch issues like missing items, breakage, or recording mistakes early.

question: How does human placental lactogen primarily help the developing fetus?

options.A: By directly oxygenating fetal blood within the intervillous space
options.B: By altering maternal metabolism to make more glucose available
options.C: By preventing maternal antibodies from attacking fetal tissues
options.D: By lubricating the birth canal in preparation for vaginal delivery

explanation: Placental lactogen acts as an antagonist to maternal insulin, ensuring that glucose stays in the bloodstream longer so it can readily cross over to nourish the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why do TB patients have to take a combination of multiple drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing any side effects
options.B: To shorten the entire treatment course to one week
options.C: To prevent the development of drug-resistant bacterial strains
options.D: To make the medication taste better for the patient

explanation: Using a mix of drugs stops the sneaky TB germs from mutating and becoming resistant to treatment. Great nursing insight!

question: What is formed right after a sperm successfully fertilizes an egg?

options.A: An unfertilized follicle
options.B: A diploid zygote
options.C: A mature blastocyst
options.D: A haploid gamete

explanation: When the sperm and egg join, they combine their chromosomes to restore a full set of 46, creating a brand new single-celled zygote ready to grow!

question: What legal charge might you face if you force medication on a clear-headed adult patient who says no?

options.A: Defamation
options.B: Battery
options.C: Invasion of privacy
options.D: Breach of contract

explanation: Exactly! Giving unwanted treatment to a competent adult who refused it counts as battery under the law. Always respect patient autonomy!

question: What happens to a student's brain when the classroom environment feels unsafe or hostile?

options.A: You suddenly feel super creative and relaxed
options.B: You focus on survival and anxiety rather than solving problems
options.C: You instantly become a great class leader
options.D: You find it twice as easy to memorize drugs

explanation: When you feel threatened or scared of being ridiculed, fear takes over, making it really hard to concentrate on learning new clinical skills.

question: How does the DRF system help protect patients from fake or substandard drugs?

options.A: By testing every single pill in a laboratory before selling it
options.B: By destroying all imported medications immediately
options.C: By purchasing drugs only from verified and approved suppliers
options.D: By allowing patients to bring their own drugs from home

explanation: Safety first! By sticking to trusted, approved suppliers, the pharmacy keeps fake medications far away from our patients.

question: Who needs to be right there at the bedside when a very early preterm baby is delivered?

options.A: The hospital administrator and billing officers
options.B: An orthopedic surgeon and surgical assistants
options.C: A specialized hospital social worker and dietician
options.D: Neonatal resuscitation and paediatric team members

explanation: Teamwork is everything in the labour ward! Having the neonatal experts ready ensures the tiny newborn gets immediate respiratory help. Fantastic clinical judgment!

question: Which compress is best for a patient who twisted their ankle just ten minutes ago?

options.A: Alternating hot and steaming compress
options.B: Room-temperature dry wrap
options.C: Cold compress
options.D: Warm compress

explanation: For fresh injuries (acute injuries), cold therapy is your best friend to keep swelling and pain down.

question: Why is qualitative feedback just as important as hard numbers when evaluating a health project?

options.A: It takes less time to collect than counting clinic cards
options.B: It guarantees that diseases will never return to the village
options.C: It is required by law for every international aid disbursement
options.D: It reveals whether the community has truly gained ownership and confidence

explanation: Qualitative insights capture people's attitudes, perceived empowerment, and behavioral changes that raw numbers might miss. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of these medications is classified as a long-acting corticosteroid?

options.A: Prednisolone
options.B: Dexamethasone
options.C: Hydrocortisone
options.D: Methylprednisolone

explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone is a long-acting steroid that stays active in the body for 36 to 72 hours. Keep up the great revision!

question: What is the main goal of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To find out which hospital ward cost the most money
options.B: To collect financial donations from family members
options.C: To monitor exposed individuals and catch new cases early
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteers

explanation: Well done! Tracking down people who were exposed lets us watch them closely and isolate them before they can spread the illness further.

question: How do association areas differ from sensory and motor areas in the brain?

options.A: They directly connect spinal nerves to peripheral skeletal muscles
options.B: They are located exclusively deep within the brain stem rather than the cortex
options.C: They only function during deep sleep and remain completely inactive while awake
options.D: They deal with complex thoughts and reasoning rather than direct input or output

explanation: Think of association areas as the brain's processing hubs—they bring different pieces of information together for high-level thinking and reasoning!

question: Where are the ureters positioned in the tummy area?

options.A: Subcutaneous position just beneath the skin
options.B: Medial position inside the peritoneal cavity
options.C: Intraperitoneal position floating near the liver
options.D: Retroperitoneal position along the posterior wall

explanation: Great try! They sit outside the main tummy cavity, running quietly down the back wall behind the peritoneum.

question: What key cellular sign helps a pathologist identify chronic endometritis under a microscope?

options.A: Complete absence of any immune cells
options.B: The presence of plasma cells in the endometrial stroma
options.C: Enlarged muscle fibers in the outer wall
options.D: An overwhelming number of red blood cells

explanation: While acute infections bring neutrophils, chronic (long-term) endometritis is officially diagnosed by spotting plasma cells hiding out in the tissue lining.

question: What is the largest organ in the human body?

options.A: The liver
options.B: The skin
options.C: The large intestine
options.D: The skeletal system

explanation: The skin covers the entire external surface of the body, making it the largest single organ by surface area and weight. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why did people in early history practice family planning?

options.A: To increase the speed of urban industrial growth
options.B: To comply with modern hospital guidelines
options.C: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.D: To manage family size and resource allocation

explanation: Even long ago, communities needed to make sure they had enough food and resources for everyone, so they practiced family planning to manage family size.

question: What do purple stretch marks (striae) on a patient's belly tell you during an endocrine assessment?

options.A: They indicate excess cortisol levels
options.B: They show sudden weight loss from diabetes
options.C: They point toward chronic low blood pressure
options.D: They signal an acute thyroid infection

explanation: Too much cortisol weakens the protein fibers in the skin, making it fragile and resulting in those distinctive purple stretch marks, often seen in conditions like Cushing's.

question: Why are patients with weak immune systems at much higher risk after an abortion procedure?

options.A: They are allergic to all surgical instruments
options.B: They absorb pain medications much faster than other patients
options.C: Their bodies cannot produce red blood cells
options.D: Their weakened defenses allow normal flora to cause severe infection

explanation: When the immune system is down, it struggles to fight off everyday bacteria that normally wouldn't cause any trouble.

question: What is often the very first sign a woman might notice with early cervical cancer?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Complete cessation of urine output
options.C: Severe swelling in both feet
options.D: Sudden loss of scalp hair

explanation: Spot on! Bleeding between periods, after intercourse, or after menopause is a classic red flag that means 'time to see a doctor.'

question: A patient vomits heavily during a cardiac arrest. What should the nurse grab right away?

options.A: The suction catheter and canister
options.B: The laryngoscope handle
options.C: The bag-valve-mask resuscitator
options.D: The endotracheal tube stylet

explanation: Well thought out! We must clear vomit immediately using suction so the airway is open and safe for breathing support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: During early development, which main germ layer gives rise to all of our muscle tissues?

options.A: Blastoderm
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: You've got this! The middle germ layer, the mesoderm, is responsible for building our skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles. Think 'M for middle and muscle!'

question: What happens if clinic staff ignore their daily logs and stock registers?

options.A: Patients will automatically receive better care from nursing staff
options.B: The government will instantly increase the facility's monthly budget
options.C: Infection control practices become strictly enforced by default
options.D: Stockouts of essential medicines may go unnoticed until supplies completely run out

explanation: Keeping daily records helps you spot when drugs are running low so you can reorder before empty shelves catch you by surprise.

question: Which of these belongs to the physical school environment?

options.A: The academic grading scale used by teachers
options.B: Safe drinking water and functional sanitation
options.C: The political affiliation of the local school board
options.D: Standardized testing schedules for final exams

explanation: Correct! The physical environment is all about tangible surroundings like clean toilets, solid buildings, and safe drinking water.

question: How can you find the median value using a finished ogive graph?

options.A: Calculate the difference between the first point and the last point
options.B: Count the total number of straight line segments in the polygon
options.C: Find the highest peak on the graph and read the number directly underneath
options.D: Locate 50 percent on the y-axis, move across to the line, and drop down to the x-axis
