question: Why is putting traditional substances like saliva or dung on a newborn's umbilical cord dangerous?

options.A: It permanently stains the baby's skin around the abdomen
options.B: It prevents the infant from absorbing breast milk
options.C: It causes the umbilical cord to fall off too quickly
options.D: It introduces harmful bacteria that can cause severe infections like tetanus

explanation: The cord stump is a direct highway to the baby's bloodstream. Unclean substances easily bring in fatal germs like tetanus or sepsis. Keep it clean and dry! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: If the local currency drops in value, making imported drugs much more expensive, what should the DRF committee do?

options.A: Keep selling remaining stock at old prices until everything is completely gone
options.B: Borrow money from patients to pay for the next batch of imported drugs
options.C: Adjust selling prices based on current replacement costs to protect the fund
options.D: Stop selling medications entirely and wait for inflation to reverse itself naturally

explanation: If you don't adjust prices during currency drops, your sales revenue won't be enough to buy the next batch of drugs.

question: What is an immunization defaulter?

options.A: A child who misses a scheduled vaccine dose
options.B: A parent who refuses all medical treatments
options.C: A health worker who forgets to order vaccines
options.D: An infant who experiences a mild vaccine reaction

explanation: A defaulter simply refers to a child who fails to show up for a scheduled vaccine or misses a dose needed to complete their immunization schedule. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: Which specialist helps patients regain the ability to swallow safely?

options.A: Speech-language pathology
options.B: Occupational therapy
options.C: Respiratory therapy
options.D: Physical therapy

explanation: Spot on. Speech therapists evaluate and treat swallowing issues (dysphagia) to keep patients safe from choking or aspiration.

question: How do most medicines actually produce their effects in our body?

options.A: By altering existing physiological processes
options.B: By changing the genetic code of human cells
options.C: By completely replacing natural body hormones
options.D: By creating entirely new cellular functions

explanation: Drugs don't usually invent brand new jobs for cells. Instead, they speed up or slow down things your body is already doing naturally!

question: Why must nurses condition ice packs before putting them in a daily vaccine carrier?

options.A: To prevent the accidental freezing of freeze-sensitive vaccines
options.B: To ensure the ice melts faster during the hot afternoon sun
options.C: To make the vaccine carrier lighter for the nurse to carry
options.D: To activate the chemical VVM label on the vaccine vials

explanation: Direct contact with rock-solid ice can freeze and ruin liquid vaccines like tetanus. Conditioning the ice keeps the temperature just right!

question: Why must wrapped instrument trays be loaded loosely inside a steam sterilizer?

options.A: To allow steam to circulate freely around every package
options.B: To stop the external indicator tape from melting off
options.C: To prevent the heavy metal trays from breaking the door
options.D: To make unloading faster for the nursing assistant

explanation: If the packs are crammed too tightly together, the steam can't reach every surface, leaving pockets where germs can survive.

question: What complication happens if a localized lung infection spreads directly into the patient's bloodstream?

options.A: Sepsis
options.B: Pulmonary embolism
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary fibrosis

explanation: When germs escape the lungs and enter the general circulation, they can trigger a body-wide, dangerous inflammatory response known as sepsis.

question: When we talk about 'nutrient quality' in a meal, what are we really looking at?

options.A: The physical weight of the food on the plate
options.B: The total number of calories in a meal
options.C: How well the body absorbs and uses food compounds
options.D: How long the food item can be stored safely

explanation: You've got this! Nutrient quality is all about how effectively your body can actually use what you eat, rather than just counting empty calories.

question: What is the primary purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To increase the cost of hospital equipment
options.B: To replace clinical judgment with rigid rules
options.C: To give doctors more administrative duties
options.D: To expand knowledge and improve patient care

explanation: Research is fundamentally about discovering new information that directly enhances how nurses care for their patients. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h1)

question: You are monitoring a woman in active labor and notice a sudden, dangerous spike in her blood pressure. Which tool helped you catch this?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Umbilical cord clamp
options.C: Surgical needle holder
options.D: Mucus extractor

explanation: The sphygmomanometer and stethoscope are your go-to tools for blood pressure checks, helping you spot risky conditions like pre-eclampsia early.

question: What is the main goal of doing a statistical test on a research hypothesis?

options.A: To calculate the exact number of patients needed for a trial
options.B: To prove the null hypothesis is always correct
options.C: To see if there is enough evidence to reject the null hypothesis
options.D: To replace the alternative hypothesis with a descriptive chart

explanation: Spot on! We test our data to see if we have enough strong proof to throw out the null hypothesis and say our intervention actually works.

question: Which of these bacterial airborne illnesses is still a major health concern across Nigeria?

options.A: Cholera
options.B: Malaria
options.C: Tuberculosis
options.D: Tetanus

explanation: Spot on! Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection that affects the lungs and remains a huge focus for public health and nursing here in Nigeria.

question: How does getting feedback from the hospital help you when you visit patients at home?

options.A: It proves to the village chief that the hospital doctors are competent
options.B: It allows the nurse to charge the patient for specialist consultation
options.C: It gives the nurse a reason to avoid seeing new clinic patients
options.D: It helps the nurse understand the final diagnosis and monitor home recovery

explanation: Spot on! Knowing the hospital's diagnosis and treatment plan lets you provide fantastic, targeted follow-up care right there in the community.

question: Why is it so important to respect a survivor's personal choices (autonomy) during care?

options.A: It legally transfers all hospital liability onto the patient
options.B: It restores a sense of personal control after experiencing trauma
options.C: It speeds up the physical wound-healing process significantly
options.D: It proves that the nursing staff lacks clinical experience

explanation: You nailed it! Abuse strips people of their power and choices. Letting them guide decisions in their care helps rebuild their confidence and trust in you. Fantastic nursing mindset!

question: Why do qualitative researchers love open-ended questions?

options.A: They make it easy to enter numbers directly into a computer
options.B: They prevent participants from talking about sensitive topics
options.C: They encourage participants to share detailed personal stories
options.D: They guarantee that every interview takes exactly five minutes

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions give people the freedom to talk in their own words, giving you rich, colourful stories instead of a simple 'yes' or 'no'.

question: A child's weight-for-length falls way below the minus two Z-score on the growth chart. What does this mean?

options.A: Advanced neurological maturity
options.B: Chronic skeletal stunting
options.C: Acute malnutrition or wasting
options.D: Normal developmental variation

explanation: You're doing great! Weight-for-length compares mass to height. A very low score means the child has recently lost weight and is too thin for their height—a sign of wasting.

question: Why should family members be included during a rehabilitation assessment?

options.A: Caregivers often notice daily challenges that clinical tests miss
options.B: Family members are legally required to sign all charts
options.C: Relatives can perform physical therapy instead of professionals
options.D: It reduces the total cost of purchasing hospital equipment

explanation: Great job! Families live closely with the patient, so they give us real-life insights that a quick check in the clinic might completely miss.

question: What is the main job of the circulating nurse during an operation?

options.A: Closing the surgical wound layers with sutures and staples
options.B: Managing the unsterile environment and monitoring patient safety
options.C: Performing the surgical incisions alongside the primary surgeon
options.D: Administering the general anesthetic gases to the patient

explanation: While the scrub nurse is sterile at the table, the circulating nurse moves freely around the room to coordinate supplies, record notes, and watch out for the patient's safety.

question: Why might a family living in severe poverty choose not to spend money on transport to a family planning clinic?

options.A: Hospitals do not allow poor people inside
options.B: Medical clinics only open during midnight hours
options.C: They prefer buying luxury items for their home
options.D: Immediate daily survival needs take priority over preventive care

explanation: Exactly. When daily food and shelter are a struggle, spending scarce cash on transport for health checkups has to wait.

question: Why is the federal VAPP Act alone sometimes not enough to stop FGM across all Nigerian states?

options.A: States must pass their own version (domesticate the act) before local courts can enforce it
options.B: Traditional rulers have complete immunity from federal laws
options.C: The federal government leaves rural areas out of national laws
options.D: Federal laws expire automatically after five years

explanation: You got it! Nigeria operates under a federal system where state legislatures must domesticate federal laws for them to be fully operational and enforceable locally.

question: Why can taking very large megadoses of fat-soluble vitamins be dangerous?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in the body and can accumulate to toxic levels
options.B: The body attacks fat-soluble vitamins as foreign bacteria and triggers shock
options.C: Excess fat-soluble vitamins instantly turn into dangerous trans fats
options.D: High doses immediately cause total kidney failure by dissolving water in blood

explanation: Spot on! Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in our body fat and liver instead of being peed out, taking too many over time can build up to dangerous levels.

question: Why is it risky to just sit back and trust bedside monitors blindly?

options.A: Bedside machines drain too much electricity from the room
options.B: Monitors can show false readings or artifact that require physical verification
options.C: Monitors are generally illegal to use without a physician present
options.D: Monitors only measure body temperature and nothing else

explanation: Machines are great helpers, but they aren't human! A simple movement can mess up the reading. Always double-check the monitor numbers by actually looking at and touching your patient.

question: A patient actively moves their arm through space without any nurse assistance. What type of movement is being tested?

options.A: Resisted range of motion
options.B: Reflexive range of motion
options.C: Active range of motion
options.D: Passive range of motion

explanation: Active range of motion occurs when the patient moves the joint entirely on their own power without outside assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which group of patients is at the highest risk of accidentally breathing in (aspirating) barium during the test?

options.A: Patients with a history of high blood pressure
options.B: Patients with severe swallowing difficulties
options.C: Patients who receive a mild laxative post-test
options.D: Patients who fasted for longer than twelve hours

explanation: Good clinical thinking! If someone already struggles to swallow, they can easily choke and pull the barium down into their lungs. Always assess carefully! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h7)

question: What happens when a patient takes two different medications that both depress the central nervous system?

options.A: Liver enzymes shut down permanently to prevent any chemical processing
options.B: An additive or synergistic sedative effect that can impair breathing
options.C: The two drugs cancel each other out completely with no effect
options.D: The patient experiences a sudden burst of high physical energy

explanation: Combining multiple depressants multiplies their calming effects on the brain and can dangerously slow breathing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is a common myth among young people regarding Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Regular screening helps catch hidden diseases
options.B: Condoms can help prevent transmission
options.C: People with STIs always look visibly sick
options.D: Some infections do not show early symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Many people are surprised to learn that numerous STIs show no early symptoms at all, meaning someone can feel completely healthy while carrying an infection.

question: What is the main goal of practicing a 'Just Culture' in nursing?

options.A: Eliminating all paperwork related to patient safety incidents
options.B: Protecting the hospital from costly medical malpractice lawsuits
options.C: Encouraging staff to report errors safely without unfair blame
options.D: Ensuring every single mistake receives a harsh suspension

explanation: Fantastic! Just Culture promotes open reporting so our hospitals can learn from mistakes instead of driving them underground. You're doing great!

question: What is a very common cause of death in babies suffering from neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Complete bone demineralization
options.B: Severe kidney failure and fluid overload
options.C: Asphyxia from respiratory muscle spasms
options.D: Massive internal gastrointestinal bleeding

explanation: Correct! Spasms in the throat and chest muscles can block the airway, quickly leading to a lack of oxygen (asphyxia) if not managed.

question: What do high-pressure alarms usually tell you about a mechanically ventilated patient?

options.A: The patient is breathing too slowly or not at all
options.B: Changes in lung compliance or increased airway resistance
options.C: A disconnection of the main tubing from the patient
options.D: A power failure in the wall electrical socket

explanation: When the high-pressure alarm sounds, it means something is making it harder to push air in—like mucus plugs, coughing, or the patient biting the tube. Time to put on your detective hat and check the patient!

question: What is considered the absolute cornerstone of youth-friendly healthcare?

options.A: Formal hospital uniforms
options.B: Expensive equipment
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Strict parental control

explanation: Guarantees of privacy and confidentiality are essential to make young people feel safe enough to share personal health details. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: What does decontamination do for a dirty surgical instrument right after use?

options.A: It achieves absolute sterility without the need for an autoclave machine
options.B: It removes organic soil and lowers bioburden so staff can handle the tool safely
options.C: It replaces the need for thorough high-level chemical disinfection
options.D: It permanently alters the metal alloy to prevent future corrosion in storage

explanation: Decontamination is your first line of defense. It washes away heavy dirt so you can handle the tools without risking an infection.

question: Why is it risky for a nurse to assume direct cause-and-effect from a simple correlational study?

options.A: It violates patient confidentiality laws in the hospital ward
options.B: It can lead to implementing ineffective or incorrect patient care practices
options.C: It means the researcher forgot to calculate the negative numbers
options.D: It guarantees that statistical software will crash during data analysis

explanation: Spot on! Acting on false assumptions can waste precious time and hospital resources on patient care interventions that don't actually work.

question: Which of the following is NOT a known complication of intrapleural drug therapy?

options.A: Systemic toxicity from drug absorption
options.B: Re-expansion pulmonary edema
options.C: Severe local pleuritic chest pain
options.D: Permanent loss of the patient's voice box

explanation: You nailed it! Intrapleural treatments deal with the chest cavity and lungs, not the larynx or vocal cords, so voice loss has nothing to do with this procedure.

question: What important advice should a nurse give a heart failure patient about managing fluids at home?

options.A: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.B: Drink at least four liters of water every single morning
options.C: Weigh yourself daily and report sudden weight gains
options.D: Avoid all physical movement to save body water

explanation: Brilliant! Stepping on the scale every day is the easiest way for a patient to catch fluid buildup before it turns into breathing trouble.

question: A patient suddenly develops severe shortness of breath and chest pain after a long plane ride. Which condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Left ventricular failure

explanation: Immobility during a long trip can lead to blood clots in the legs that break off and travel to the lungs, causing a pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the main sterol found in the cell membrane of fungi?

options.A: Peptidoglycan
options.B: Cholesterol
options.C: Chitin
options.D: Ergosterol

explanation: Spot on! Fungal cell membranes use ergosterol. This is super helpful in pharmacology because many antifungal drugs target ergosterol, leaving our human cells (which use cholesterol) alone.

question: What do we really mean by 'motivation' when managing a nursing team?

options.A: The financial bonus given at the end of the year
options.B: The physical strength required to complete a shift
options.C: The internal drive that pushes a worker to take action
options.D: The strict set of rules enforced by the hospital board

explanation: Spot on! Motivation is that inner spark or energy that pushes us to chase our goals and get things done on the ward.

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a community health education program?

options.A: To create unnecessary paperwork for the local government health office
options.B: To punish community members who failed to attend the teaching sessions
options.C: To prove that the nurse is smarter than the people in the village
options.D: To determine if the program achieved its goals and identify areas for improvement

explanation: Correct! Evaluation helps you see what worked well and what you can do better next time.

question: How many primary lobes make up the glandular tissue of a human breast?

options.A: 2 to 5

explanation: A mature human breast typically contains 15 to 20 glandular lobes arranged radially around the nipple. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h3)

question: What is the main job of government policies in healthcare?

options.A: Deciding which patients get admitted to private rooms
options.B: Manufacturing all pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.C: Personally training every nurse and doctor in the country
options.D: Determining service prioritization, funding, and accessibility

explanation: Government policies set the rules for how money is shared and whether health services actually reach the people who need them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to care for an FGM survivor in the clinic?

options.A: Reporting the adult patient to local police immediately
options.B: Inspecting the surgical site without warning the patient
options.C: Refusing to discuss the cultural background of the practice
options.D: Using a trauma-informed and non-judgmental approach

explanation: Great choice! Trauma-informed care builds trust, lowers anxiety, and makes sure the patient feels safe and respected.

question: As a nurse, why should you understand lab values instead of just looking at the high or low flags?

options.A: Because laboratory printers frequently misprint the normal reference ranges
options.B: Because nurses are legally required to diagnose medical diseases
options.C: Because numbers help the nurse anticipate complications and plan safer care
options.D: Because doctors do not look at blood reports until discharge

explanation: You're not just memorizing numbers for an exam! Connecting lab values to real body signs helps you spot trouble early and keep your patient safe.

question: Which medication is used in medical abortion to cause strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Ergometrine
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Misoprostol helps the uterus contract and safely push out any remaining tissue. You'll see this drug used a lot in ward practice!

question: Why must a National Drug Policy tie in closely with the National Health Policy?

options.A: It allows pharmaceutical companies to set their own market prices without government interference.
options.B: International donors will refuse to release funds if the two policies are separate documents.
options.C: Medications are essential therapeutic tools required to achieve overall population health goals.
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to purchase hospital supplies out of their own pockets.

explanation: You can't achieve a healthy nation without medicines! Because drugs are our most common tool for treatment, the drug policy has to support the country's bigger health goals.

question: Which of these is a great example of a drug working without using a receptor?

options.A: An insulin molecule attaching to a muscle cell
options.B: An opioid binding to a brain pain receptor
options.C: A beta-blocker slowing down the heart rate
options.D: An osmotic laxative pulling water into the bowel

explanation: Spot on! Osmotic laxatives rely on physical water movement rather than locking onto cellular receptors to do their job.
